source_documents.title: Twisted intramolecular charge transfer in betaine B30

reference_evidence_units.quote: the lowest excited singlet state of B30 can relax to a twisted conformation in which fluorescence and stimulated emission are forbidden
reference_evidence_units.subject: B30
reference_evidence_units.statement: S1 relaxes to a twisted, non-emissive conformation.

reference_evidence_units.quote: A decrease in the calculated oscillator strength to essentially zero explains the absence of radiative transitions in the twisted conformation
reference_evidence_units.subject: B30

reference_evidence_units.quote: The requirement for a substantial reorganization of the surrounding solvent rationalizes the increase of fluorescence at low temperatures and viscous media.
reference_evidence_units.subject: B30
reference_evidence_units.statement: Slowed twisting/solvent reorganisation in viscous or cold media lets fluorescence appear.

reference_mechanisms.label: RIM_RIR_RIV
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Fluorescence appears in viscous or frozen media where the twisting relaxation is slowed (molecular-rotor rule).

reference_mechanisms.label: ICT_TICT_CT
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Relaxation of the charge-transfer S1 state to a twisted (TICT) conformation is the paper's subject.

reference_mechanisms.label: RADIATIVE_RATE_STATE_BALANCE
reference_mechanisms.rationale: The twisted state is dark because its oscillator strength drops to ~0 (calculation).
